speaker: Doctor
text:
The urinalysis shows white blood cells but no red blood cells or protein, suggesting inflammation in the urinary tract, while your rheumatoid factor is normal. Given your history of recurrent joint swelling in the knee and ankle, have these joint episodes been symmetrical or did they affect one joint at a time?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The HLA-B27 test results are normal, which makes seronegative spondyloarthropathies less likely, though not impossible. To further clarify the pattern of your joint inflammation, were your previous ankle and current knee episodes monoarticular (affecting only one joint) or did they involve multiple joints simultaneously?

REQUEST TEST: ESR (Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate)
REQUEST TEST: CRP (C-Reactive Protein)

speaker: Doctor
text:
The ESR is elevated at 38 mm/h, indicating active inflammation. Based on your history of recurrent monoarticular joint swelling in the knee and ankle, combined with sterile pyuria (white blood cells in urine without bacteria or protein), do you have a history of recent gastrointestinal infections like diarrhea or blood in your stool?

REQUEST TEST: Stool_Culture
REQUEST TEST: ANA (Antinuclear Antibody)

speaker: Doctor
text: The ANA and Stool Culture results are normal, which makes systemic lupus erythemathematosus and reactive arthritis secondary to gut infection less likely. Given the pattern of recurrent monoarticular joint swelling in the knee and ankle, combined with sterile pyuria and an elevated ESR, do you have a history of recurrent genital or oral herpes simplex virus infections?
